page: Amazon Web Services d2.xlarge is a dense storage-optimized virtual machine running on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by a 64-bit Intel Xeon E5-2676 v3 processor clocked at 2.4 GHz, utilizing two physical cores with hyper-threading to deliver 4 dedicated vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 30.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 7.62 GB per physical core. Its defining feature is 6,144 GB of integrated local HDD storage, supported by a 1 Gbps baseline network connection. The platform does not incorporate discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results highlight an architecture oriented toward storage capacity rather than high-throughput compute. In CPU processing evaluations, the instance registers a stress-ng single-core score of 738.49 and a multi-core score of 2077.66, along with a Geekbench multi-core result of 1880.0, placing its raw compute within the lower performance tiers. Memory tests show uncached large-block read bandwidth of 26.52 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 16.66 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates 1.25 million Redis SET operations per second and static web serving throughput of 2.81 GB/sec.

The qualitative value of the d2.xlarge is centered on dense, cost-effective magnetic disk storage capacity rather than high IOPS or compute density. Deploying over six terabytes of local HDD space makes this instance type practical for sequential data ingestion, Hadoop or MapReduce worker nodes, distributed file system architectures, and log aggregation tasks where large-volume storage outweighs CPU-intensive performance demands.
description: Amazon Web Services d2.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance tailored for workloads requiring significant local rotational storage. The server provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores utilizing an Intel Xeon E5-2676 v3 processor running at 2.4 GHz, alongside 30.0 GB of system memory. Its primary architectural feature is 6,144 GB of direct-attached HDD storage, paired with a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and no hardware GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show entry-tier CPU performance, with stress-ng scores of 738.49 single-core and 2077.66 multi-core, complemented by moderate memory bandwidth. The instance trades compute density and solid-state IOPS for bulk local data capacity, delivering strong qualitative cost efficiency for sequential read and write operations. The d2.xlarge is engineered primarily for distributed file storage, MapReduce cluster nodes, data warehousing, and log archival tasks requiring large local disk volumes.
